name: Sahibe ulaşma omurgası
what_this_proves: The system can now reach the owner with the browser closed, and can say honestly when it could not. Before this batch every notification path ended either in a page nobody had open or in the fake push transport's in-memory log, so 'the owner has been told' was true only while they were already looking - and false again after every restart.

closed_fully.367_durable_table: The queue was a `deque` in one process's memory. The row is written to `notifications` BEFORE any delivery is attempted, so a restart mid-ladder loses an attempt and never a notification. 18 columns, one migration (0044), and the attempt record lives on the row rather than in a call stack - which is what makes the ladder resumable rather than restartable.
closed_fully.368_inbox: Two halves. `/v1/notifications` reads the table and asks no transport what it remembers, and the cockpit's Bildirimler panel prints THREE states rather than one: `hiçbir kanal taşımadı`, `iletildi, okunmadı`, `okundu`. Collapsing them is how a system convinces itself it communicated - a toast that appeared on a locked screen at 03:00 reached the machine, not the owner.
closed_fully.369_desktop_toast: Written as a contract first (`packages/protocol/desktop-notify.json`), because the last four capabilities that were not - file.search roots, the app manifest, the native manifest, the device protocol schema - each shipped with both suites green and neither half able to talk to the other. Both halves read the contract's own numbers: the Cloud Core's length limits come from `contract()["request"][field]["max_chars"]`, and `DesktopNotifyContractTests.cs` reads the same file. Registered in `test_contract_falsification.py` with its `held_by`/`unheld` pair.
closed_fully.377_delivery_history: `/v1/notifications/history` lists what NOTHING carried alongside what was delivered. That is the part of a delivery history worth reading: a channel that has never once worked looks exactly like a device that happened to be switched off, until you can see the rows nothing reached.
closed_fully.378_priority: Three levels. An unknown value falls to `normal` rather than creating a fourth level, and each of the eight events records WHY it has the priority it has (B12) - because `urgent` is a decision to wake somebody, and a priority nobody has to justify drifts upward until the owner turns the whole thing off.
closed_fully.379_quiet_hours: 23:00-07:30, midnight wrap handled. Deliberately about NOISE and not about hiding: a deferred row is in the inbox the whole time and is visible there; only the interruption waits for morning. Urgent is exempt, which is the entire content of the word.
closed_fully.380_grouping: Supersedes the UNREAD sibling in the same group only. A read sibling is something the owner already knows about, and quietly replacing it would erase a thing they had seen. Seven nights of the same failed backup leave one unread notice saying so.
closed_fully.389_ladder: toast -> sound -> push -> inbox, with the inbox as the floor, so the ladder cannot fail - it can only end with the owner finding out later than the system would have liked. A rung that cannot be tried is skipped rather than waited for; a rung already tried is never tried again for the same row, or the ladder is a loop.

not_claimed_done.369_370_partial: PARTIAL, not DONE. Both halves exist and are wired, the balloon is a real Windows shell notification, and the action buttons are parsed, carried and refused correctly when malformed - but `ShellToastSink` is a NotifyIcon balloon and has no action buttons, which the device says in its own answer's `detail` rather than pretending. REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED for this batch is a locked screen with the browser closed, and that needs the agent installed on the owner's machine.
not_claimed_done.372_webpush: BLOCKED_OWNER. The client half (a service worker) was never written and payload encryption needs a VAPID key pair the owner must generate. Writing a transport that cannot be keyed would put a rung on the ladder that is guaranteed to say no - noise, and worse, a rung an operator would reasonably believe had been tried.

defects_found_on_the_way.the_ladder_had_no_caller: `ladder.sweep` was written and NOTHING called it - the same 'written but unwired' defect the B12 guard had caught minutes earlier for `backup_failed`, and the one this repository has now paid for six times (three retention sweeps, a speaker verdict, a reconcile timer, this). Wired into `RetentionSweeper` in `create_app`, where a test can enumerate it.
defects_found_on_the_way.the_toast_rung_called_a_signature_that_d: The rung passed `device_id=` and `trace_id=` to `DeviceActionPort.run`, which takes neither. Every toast would have raised `TypeError` inside the ladder's catch-all and been recorded as a device that did not show it: a channel that never worked, looking exactly like a device switched off. The hand-rolled rung doubles could not see it, because a double accepts whatever it is passed. The regression drives the REAL rung against `create_autospec(DeviceActionPort)`, so a keyword the rung invents raises here.
defects_found_on_the_way.the_capability_was_spelled_twice: `desktop.notify` was added to the C# `Ambient` group and never declared on the Cloud Core side, so `test_desktop_capability_mirror` failed exactly as designed ('the agent declares desktop names this reconciliation does not know about'). Cloud Core now declares `CAPABILITY_DESKTOP_NOTIFY` as `toast.CAPABILITY` rather than restating the string, and a test asserts the contract file, the notifications half and the dispatch table all say the same word.
defects_found_on_the_way.the_gate_step_i_added_never_ran: The `-Fast` gate's other-services ruff step, added in d7f726a to stop CI finding what the local gate missed, had its two paths written with backslash separators and a string literal on the way in turned them into a carriage return and a backspace: `services<CR>ecovery-supervisor` and `services<BS>rowser`. `Push-Location` then failed or silently left the shell at the repo root, `ruff check .` ran there, and the step printed 'All checks passed!' about two trees it had never entered. Fixed with forward slashes - which no escape layer can mangle - and a `Test-Path` guard, so a path that is not there throws instead of passing. A step written to stop a silent pass had become one.
defects_found_on_the_way.two_sweeps_the_guards_caught: `test_health_endpoint.py` and `test_maintenance.py` both failed on the two new sweeps, which is what they are for: health NAMES every registered sweep and the maintenance test asserts the APPLICATION reaches each one. Registering a sweep without appearing in both is impossible, which is the guard B06 built after three sweeps shipped with no caller.

red_first.method: app/notifications/ladder.py copied to a backup with its sha256, the shipped bug re-introduced, the suite re-run, restored by digest verification (`sha256sum -c`: OK).
red_first.toast_rung: 3 failed / 33 deselected with the wrong kwargs restored - `TypeError: got an unexpected keyword argument 'device_id'` from the autospec, which is precisely the error the blanket except was swallowing in production.
red_first.capability_mirror: The mirror test failed on its own before the Cloud Core constant existed: 'the agent declares desktop names this reconciliation does not know about: [desktop.notify]'.

runtime_proof.why: REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED for B11 is a toast appearing with the browser closed and the screen locked, and staying in the inbox afterwards. That needs the agent build installed on the owner's machine (OWNER_ACTION on the roadmap's own risk line) and is carried forward with Karar 0.

ci_note: The push at 86769d7 went red on the Windows agent job: `desktop.notify` broke two guards the local -Fast gate did not run - the C# manifest pin (db84bbd) and the staged-update qualification's hard capability count (8d2d56e). Both are fixed, both now run in -Fast, and this run is green on the tree that carries all three commits. Recorded rather than tidied away: the batch's own evidence is where a red CI belongs.
